clue.text: Teacher of law making points about translation

indicators.note: about means the compass points are placed around the other piece

parts.note: S and E are two compass points, south and east
a crib is a literal translation used by students

explanation.surface: Someone who teaches law is busy doing a translation with a few points around it.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible the scribes were the teachers of Jewish law.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels the scribes were the scholars who taught and interpreted Jewish religious law.

clue.text: Representation of a shipper in stone

indicators.note: a representation of something renders it in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carving of a shipper made in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious gemstone, usually blue.

clue.text: Sort of tide came first round pierhead and ruffled the surface

indicators.note: round means the pair of words that come before are put around the head of the pier

parts.note: a rip is a rough current or tide race
led means came first, was in front
the head of the word pier is its first letter, P

explanation.surface: A tide swirling round the end of a pier stirs up the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Small waves disturbed the water, the sense of rippled as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Social gathering at which one is required to call

definitions.text: Social gathering at which one is required to call

parts.words: Social gathering at which one is required to call
parts.note: reads like a visit you are obliged to pay, but describes a country dance where a caller shouts out the steps

explanation.surface: A party you are expected to visit out of social duty.
explanation.definitionFit: At a country dance held in a rural hall, a caller announces each figure for the dancers.

clue.text: The first man to wield a pen in Egypt's lake district

indicators.note: to wield is read as to hold, so the first man holds the bird inside him

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Adam, the first man to write with a pen, did so in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is the female swan; the A before it is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The barrage on the Nile near Aswan created Lake Nasser, so it dominates that lake region of Egypt.

clue.text: Great guide, but one lacking resistance when very chilly

definitions.text: one lacking resistance when very chilly

parts.note: super means great, excellent
a conductor guides, as on a tour or an orchestra

explanation.surface: A wonderful tour guide who somehow puts up no resistance when the weather turns freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain materials lose all electrical resistance when cooled close to absolute zero.

clue.text: Chancellor once declaiming a party line, loudly

parts.note: a do is a party
F, forte, means loudly in music

explanation.surface: A former German chancellor ranting out a party line at full volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitler, first name Adolf, became German Chancellor in 1933.

clue.text: So-called humble domain

indicators.note: so-called means as it is called or spoken, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to demean is to humble, lower someone

explanation.surface: A modest little territory that only goes by that name.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb humble gives DEMEAN, which shares its sound with a word for a landed estate (one pronunciation rhymes with mean).
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held as one's own, an estate or realm.

clue.text: Mood as pronounced in Middle English

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: oral means spoken, pronounced aloud

explanation.surface: A feeling as it was expressed in medieval English.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the spirit or confidence of a person or group.

clue.text: Be the third party and act the fool perhaps

parts.note: to play is to act
a fool is a creamy fruit pudding, and gooseberry fool is the classic one

explanation.surface: To be the third wheel on a date and behave like an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' suggests a clown, but here it is the British dessert of puréed fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: To play gooseberry is the British idiom for being an unwanted third person with a couple.

clue.text: It keeps reports together in part of the press box

parts.note: a newspaper is one part of the press
to box someone's ears is to clip them, hit them

explanation.surface: Something that holds the news stories together in the reporters' gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent wire fastener holds sheets of a report together.

clue.text: Mollusc, or merely part of it?

indicators.note: part of means the letters are a section of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Is this sea creature only a fragment of something?
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an abalone, a shellfish found around the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Billie's given a break

definitions.meaning: a vacation, time off from work

explanation.surface: A singer gets a little time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie Holiday was the American jazz singer; a holiday is time away from work.

clue.text: Unwillingness to jump at an option

definitions.meaning: a horse that stops at a fence makes a ...
first ... is an option to buy before others

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to leap at a chance offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse balking at a jump commits this fault; first refusal is a right to buy before others.

clue.text: The thinking man's sculptor

parts.note: reads as an artist for intellectuals, but means the sculptor of the famous bronze of a man deep in thought

explanation.surface: An artist beloved of intellectuals.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin sculpted Le Penseur, the seated figure lost in thought.

clue.text: The counter for travel information

parts.note: suggests a tourist information desk, but means a device that counts the distance travelled

explanation.surface: The desk where you ask about journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: A mileage gauge in a car records how far it has gone.

clue.text: Comfortable times for teachers in never-never land

definitions.text: Comfortable times for teachers in never-never land

parts.words: Comfortable times for teachers in never-never land
parts.note: reads as relaxed school terms for teachers in a fantasy world, but never-never is British slang for hire purchase, bought by instalments

explanation.surface: Teachers enjoying relaxed school periods in Peter Pan's world.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous instalment arrangements for buying goods on credit, the never-never being hire purchase.

clue.text: Leaves, maybe having grizzled about Frenchman's rise

indicators.note: about means the grey-haired word goes around the other piece

parts.note: grizzled means grey-haired

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Foliage, perhaps, given that a grey-haired man surrounded a Frenchman as he got up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the plural noun; in a down clue 'rise' means the Frenchman's name is written bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves are an example of green plant growth, which is what greenery means.

clue.text: Got into debt, at first, following "expert' about tax

indicators.note: following means the first letter of debt comes after the rest
about means the word for expert goes around the tax word

parts.note: an ace is an expert
cess is an old word for a tax or levy

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone fell into debt from the start after an expert dealt with their tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To have accessed somewhere is to have gained entry, the same as entered.

clue.text: Agreeable medicine

definitions.meaning: originally a stimulating medicinal drink for the heart

explanation.surface: A pleasant-tasting remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and friendly, and historically names a reviving tonic drink.

clue.text: Term of affection for such a daddy

definitions.meaning: a pet name like honey or sweetie
a rich older man who lavishes gifts on a younger partner is this kind of daddy

explanation.surface: A loving nickname for a certain kind of father.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an endearment like honey, and a wealthy older benefactor is this kind of daddy.

clue.text: Actress seen to rip paper up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the two words are read from the bottom, each turned in place

parts.note: to rend is to rip
a rag is slang for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A film star is spotted tearing up a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole of RENDRAG backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood star of the 1940s and 1950s.

clue.text: Gem that is a horse, perhaps

parts.note: sc., scilicet, is Latin for that is, namely
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A jewel which turns out to be a horse, possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab is a gem carved in the form of a beetle, as in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: It may, be smoked to preserve coal

parts.note: to corn is to preserve with salt, as in corned beef
a cob is a rounded lump of coal

explanation.surface: Something smoked, maybe, to keep coal from going off.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray comma after 'may' is a misprint in the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob pipe is a tobacco pipe whose bowl is made from a maize cob.

clue.text: Battle in which men from the : ranks can gain promotion

definitions.text: Battle in which men from the : ranks can gain promotion

parts.words: Battle in which men from the : ranks can gain promotion
parts.note: sounds like a war where ordinary soldiers win advancement, but describes a board game where pawns reaching the last row become queens

explanation.surface: A war where common soldiers can rise to high rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is a stray mark on the page. Pawns are the men in the front rank, and one reaching the far side is promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: In this board game a pawn reaching the far rank is upgraded to another piece.

clue.text: Group of acquaintances shelter by the lake

parts.note: a cot is a small shelter or cottage
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Friends gather in a hut beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people with shared interests.

clue.text: Contact by radio beams, say

indicators.note: say signals that a word is to be heard as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Making contact over the airwaves via beams, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone on the radio is to get them to respond.

clue.text: Ordering a trip to border river

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling and tumbling, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Arranging a trip to a frontier river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'trip' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande forms much of the border between the United States and Mexico.

clue.text: Speculator's ability to recognize a hit

parts.note: a bull is a stock-market speculator who expects prices to rise
an eye for something is the ability to spot it

explanation.surface: A trader's knack for spotting a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike in the centre of the target scores the top mark in darts or archery.

clue.text: Bird seen round small quarry

parts.note: O is round in shape
quarry means hunted prey

explanation.surface: A bird spotted circling a little prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey.
